batch: MiTeC Paradox Data Editor package candidate and scope reconciliation

scopeDecision.currentDecision: The user's 2026-10-27 decision selects the full MiTeC publisher collection unless a product is end-of-life or a reproducible material source/product error makes migration unsuitable.
scopeDecision.supersedes: The earlier 2026-10-22 drop of Paradox Data Editor from v3 candidate scope.
scopeDecision.installationBoundary: This candidate retrieves and invokes the publisher installer. It does not mirror or redistribute the installer, and it is not selected by a default profile.

publisher.behavior: Paradox table viewer/editor using BDE, with password-protection removal, repair, conversion, import, export and BLOB viewing.
publisher.historicalPageLicenseText: Free for private, educational and non-commercial purposes; purchase required for other use.

retainedArtifact.digestSource: Locally rehashed retained publisher artifact; matches the 2026-10-21 frozen static extraction evidence.

candidate.repositoryValidation: Passed: 450 operations, 8 groups, 5 profiles and 304 PowerShell files.
candidate.directSourceAssertions: Passed: catalog identity, package version, retained evidence digest, local artifact digest and pending target state.
candidate.pesterSuite: Not run: the available Pester module is 3.4.0; the test is authored for Pester 5 and the attempted Pester 5 invocation could not be executed.
candidate.nativeAcceptance: Deferred: no VM state was queried or changed during this batch.

acceptanceGates: Reacquire and verify current direct-download bytes.
Use disposable Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 VMs to verify exact install, repeat, uninstall, saved-state recovery and non-owned data preservation.
Verify installer and uninstaller silent behavior, display-name matching, BDE registration/coexistence and exact recovery before target promotion.
Use synthetic Paradox data only; never open or modify a real user database.

estimates.reasonUnchanged: This is an individually selectable source-ready candidate; native install/removal/recovery and target acceptance remain open, so no whole legacy product outcome closes.
